title: Bhutan Horizons | From Dzongs to Himalayan Peaks
highlights: Explore Bhutan’s capital, Thimphu, with visits to the Simtokha Dzong and Buddha Dordenma, offering insights into Bhutanese traditions and the country’s rich architecture.
Wander through the Phobjikha Valley, known to be the winter home to the globally threatened black-necked cranes that migrate here from the Tibetan Plateau.
Marvel at the majestic Punakha Dzong, Bhutan’s former capital, celebrated for its exquisite woodwork and serene riverside views.
Embark on a serene journey through Bhutan's scenic landscapes, witnessing rich culture, iconic sights, and creating unforgettable memories.
Enjoy a scenic hike to the legendary Tiger’s Nest Monastery, perched dramatically on a cliffside at 9,678 feet, where Guru Rinpoche is believed to have meditated.
overview:
About the tour:
Embark on a captivating 10-day journey through the mystical landscapes and cultural treasures of Bhutan. This thoughtfully curated tour offers a deep exploration of Bhutan's scenic beauty, rich traditions, and peaceful way of life.
Widely recognised as the 'happiest country in the world', Bhutan is one of only two carbon-neutral countries, making it a true haven for nature lovers. As you journey through its breathtaking landscapes, you’ll find serenity and awe at every turn. Each day in this magical land will leave you with memories to cherish for a lifetime.

know_before_you_go: Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.
It is wise to carry enough cash, especially for remote areas in the Ngultrum (BTN) currency.
Kindly carry a valid photo ID proof. PAN Card will not be considered valid identity proof.
Travellers aren't expected to wear the traditional kira, but you should make sure your clothing covers your arms and legs when entering a Dzong.
Images are for representation purposes only.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: Upon arrival at Siliguri Railway Station/Airport, get driven to your hotel in Phuntsholing for check-in. Then, spend the rest of the day at leisure, where you can relax or explore the different attractions of the city on your own. You can explore Tashi Chholing Shedra, a Buddhist educational institution, or admire the stunning Bhutanese architecture of the Bhutan Gate. Also, you can visit Gumpha mandir and witness its colorful murals, statues of deities, and intricate carvings.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Leisure Day
days.desc: After check out, get driven to the immigration office and obtain your travel permit. Then, get driven to Thimphu and upon arrival, check into your hotel. Spend the rest of your day at leisure, where you can explore the Dechen Phodrang Monastery and marvel at its stunning architecture or visit the Clock Tower Square. Also, you can admire the traditional crafts of Bhutan at the National Institute or savor authentic Bhutanese dishes at the Ambient Café, known for its stunning vibes!

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, explore Thimphu on a sightseeing tour and visit the National Memorial Chorten, one of the most visible religious structures in Thimphu. Next, explore the Motithang Takin Preserve, home to Bhutan's national animal, the takin. Continue to the Handicrafts Emporium, where you can admire traditional Bhutanese art and crafts while learning about the rich cultural heritage. Also, you can admire the innovative 3D and talking stamps at the Bhutan Postal Museum before getting driven to your hotel.

days.title: Transfer to Nubding | En Route Visit Dochula Pass and Wangdue Phodrang
days.desc: Today, after checking out of your hotel, embark on a scenic journey to Nubding. En route, make a stop at the famous Dochula Pass, known for its 108 memorial chortens (memorial/tomb), and soak in the stunning views of the Himalayas. Next, visit the Wangdue Phodrang Dzong, an amazing fortress offering glimpses of Bhutanese history and architecture. After the visit, continue your drive to Nubding. Upon your arrival, check in to the hotel and enjoy your comfortable overnight stay.

days.title: Trip to Gangtey | Transfer to Punakha
days.desc: After check-out, board your transfer for a day trip to Gangtey. Begin with a visit to the Gangtey Gompa Monastery, an ancient Buddhist monastery offering stunning views of the surrounding valley. Continue to explore the Phobjikha Valley, renowned for its scenic beauty and as the winter home of the globally threatened black-necked cranes. After the tour, you’ll get transferred to Punakha and check in to your hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Punakha Sightseeing Tour | Transfer to Paro
days.desc: Post check-out, enjoy a sightseeing tour of Punakha. Begin by visiting the Chimi Lhakhang Temple, a sacred site known as the "Fertility Temple." Continue to the Punakha Dzong, a stunning fortress nestled between two rivers (Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu), offering a glimpse into Bhutanese history. Also, walk through the famous Punkha Suspension Bridge & get a chance to opt for a thrilling river rafting at the Pho Chu Mo Chu River. Later, get driven to Paro & check in to your hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Hike to Tiger's Nest Monastery
days.desc: Begin your day with a scenic drive to Satsam Chencho Tshongkhang, the starting point of the Tiger’s Nest Trek. Once there, trek along pine-fringed trails adorned with fluttering prayer flags, with views of the cliff-hugging monastery. Upon reaching the top, discover its sacred chambers, vibrant murals, and meditation caves honoring Guru Rinpoche. Later, descend back and get driven to your hotel. Later, you can indulge in a soothing Hot Stone bath or enjoy a hearty meal at Park 76 Cafe & Pub.

days.title: Day Trip to Haa Valley
days.desc: Today, board your transfer from the hotel for a scenic excursion to Haa Valley. En route, cross the breathtaking 13,083 ft Chele La Pass, where you can take a stop to admire panoramic views of the towering Himalayas. As you continue your journey through the forested hills and alpine meadows, soak in the beauty of the Haa Valley. Once there, visit the sacred Lhakhang Karpo, known as the “White Temple,” symbolizing purity and the Lhakhang Nagpo, or the “Black Temple,” believed to rest on a lake.

days.title: Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: In the morning, check out of the hotel and get driven to Phuntsholing. Upon arrival, check in at the hotel and spend the rest of your day at leisure, where you can visit the Karbandi Monastery, perched above Phuentsholing, housing statues of Guru Rinpoche and Shakyamuni Buddha. Also, you can visit Zangto Pelri Lhakhang, a temple said to represent Guru Rinpoche’s celestial paradise, or enjoy a brewery tour, where you can enjoy craft beer tasting while learning about unique brewing traditions.
